messages.subject: DIF Test with 3 Factor Model?
parts:
Hi,

DISCLAIMER: I'm new to DIF and MIRT, so please forgive my ignorance of even the most basic terminology, concepts, and scripts.

I'm trying to conduct a DIF using the MultipleGroup function. I was able to do it for a simple 1 factor model (see first script below and attached PISA_SCIE_DIF_R Console_v123113.txt file), but unfortunately am not able to get it to work for a 3 factor model with the same dataset (see second script below and PISA_SCIE_DIF_R Console_v010114_v3Factors.txt file). I've also attached my R script for reference (PISA_SCIE_DIF_v010114_v3Factors.R).

NOTE: I began the analysis prior to the development of the new DIF function and had challenges getting that function to work. So, I decided to continue using the MultipleGroup function. Any help getting this new DIF function to work would also be greatly appreciated!

SCRIPT 1: ONE FACTOR MODEL

##### Read Data for each group

library(mirt)

# Load/read the data from each group

pisa_LL = read.table('/Users/esgsr3/Desktop/PISA_vLL.txt')

pisa_NonLL = read.table('/Users/esgsr3/Desktop/PISA_vNonLL.txt')

# Combine 2 group datasets into 1 dataset

pisa = rbind(pisa_LL, pisa_NonLL)

# Name columns of dataset

names(pisa) = c('item1','item2','item3','item4','item5',

                'item6','item7','item8','item9','item10',

                'item11','item12','item13','item14','item15',

                 'item16','item17','item18','item19','item20',

                 'item21','item22','item23','item24','item25',

                 'item26','item27','item28','item29','item30',

                  'item31','item32','item33','item34','item35')

# Select Item Variables

myvars = (pisa[ ,1:35])

head(myvars)

#summary of data to verify data is good

summary(pisa)

# Create grouping variable: CAN USE DIFFERENT SAMPLE SIZES

group <- c(rep('LL', 3148), rep('NonLL', 3148))

### DIF test for each item (using all other items as anchors)

library(mirt)

#Scans/reads user input to specify the confirmatory model: ONE (1) factor model

cmodel <- mirt.model('F1 = 1-35')

#Original Model with NO CONSTRAINTS

itemtype = c('2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','gpcm','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','gpcm','2PL','2PL','2PL')  

Origmodel.pars <- multipleGroup(pisa, cmodel, group = group, itemtype = itemtype, pars = 'values')  

Origmodel.pars

Origmodel <- multipleGroup(pisa, cmodel, group = group, itemtype = itemtype, quadpts = 21, D = 1)

coef(Origmodel)

#Item Characteristic Curve

itemplot(Origmodel, item = 1, type = "trace")

#Item Information

itemplot(Origmodel, item = 1, type = "info")

#Test Information

plot(Origmodel, type = 'info')

#Item Characteristic Curve

itemplot(Origmodel, item = 16, type = "trace")

#Item Information

itemplot(Origmodel, item = 16, type = "info")

#Test Information

plot(Origmodel, type = 'info')

#Baseline Model with FULL CONSTRAINTS

#Specifies specific item name bundles (from colnames(data)) will constrain all freely estimated parameters in each item to be equal across groups. This is useful for selecting ’anchor’ items for vertical and horizontal scaling, and for detecting differential item functioning (DIF) across groups

itemnames <- colnames(pisa) 

itemtype = c('2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','gpcm','2PL',

'2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL','2PL',

'2PL','gpcm','2PL','2PL','2PL')   

refmodel.pars <- multipleGroup(pisa, cmodel, group = group, itemtype = itemtype, pars = 'values',

                          invariance=c('free_means', 'free_varcov', itemnames))

refmodel.pars

refmodel <- multipleGroup(pisa, cmodel, group = group, itemtype = itemtype, quadpts = 21, D = 1,                         

                          invariance=c('free_means', 'free_varcov', itemnames))

coef(refmodel)

messages.subject: Re: DIF Test with 3 Factor Model?
parts:
What is happening here is that the multidimensional multiple group
model is not identified. Consider the following code from the
multipleGroup example help file:

####
library(mirt)
a <- matrix(c(abs(rnorm(5,1,.3)), rep(0,15),abs(rnorm(5,1,.3)),
rep(0,15),abs(rnorm(5,1,.3))), 15, 3)
d <- matrix(rnorm(15,0,.7),ncol=1)
mu <- c(-.4, -.7, .1)
sigma <- matrix(c(1.21,.297,1.232,.297,.81,.252,1.232,.252,1.96),3,3)
itemtype <- rep('dich', nrow(a))
N <- 1000
dataset1 <- simdata(a, d, N, itemtype)
dataset2 <- simdata(a, d, N, itemtype, mu = mu, sigma = sigma)
dat <- rbind(dataset1, dataset2)
group <- c(rep('D1', N), rep('D2', N))

#group models
model <- mirt.model('
F1 = 1-5
F2 = 6-10
F3 = 11-15')

#define mirt cluster to use parallel architecture
mirtCluster()

#EM approach (not as accurate with 3 factors, but generally good for
quick model comparisons)
mod_configural <- multipleGroup(dat, model, group = group) #completely
separate analyses
mod_metric <- multipleGroup(dat, model, group = group,
invariance=c('slopes')) #equal slopes
mod_fullconstrain <- multipleGroup(dat, model, group = group, #equal
means, slopes, intercepts
invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts'))
mod_notidentified <- multipleGroup(dat, model, group = group, #equal
means, slopes, intercepts
invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts',
'free_means', 'free_var'))
###

The first three models appear to converge well, and when you estimate
an information matrix for them all appear to behave just fine (the
dev/next major release provides a second order tests for model
convergence now for determining if a model has converged or is even
identified). More importantly, the EM history steadily increase to a
maximum, also indicating that the model is fine. However, the last
model does not converge smoothly since in the last 10-20 iterations
you can see the log-likelihood start to increase....which
theoretically never should happen unless something is amiss. Running a
second order test with the dev version shows that the information
matrix is exactly singular, and therefore the model is not identified.

I believe for the package I was too hasty with including easy-to-use
invariance commands for multidimensional multiple group models
('free_var' and 'free_varcov' especially), so I'll have to rethink
what to do about this. In the meantime, I would recommend avoiding the
free_var like commands, and pay attention to the EM convergence
history (or update to the dev version and check the information
condition). Another trick is to use the MHRM estimation, and see what
that history looks like as well; the MHRM method tends to make
non-identified models much more obvious. Cheers.

Phil
